title: Restore a shutterâ€™s contact edge and prove it reverses at both ends
instruction: Restore the shutter's contact edge and use the orange proof block to demonstrate reversal at both white marks.
context: A service shutter can reopen at one end and press into a trapped hand at the other. Demonstrate that the repaired edge protects both marked positions on a captive bench trainer.
setup: On the calibrated YAM station, mount the base at x=335 mm, y=0, on the tabletop. Two green spring-loaded shoes run across the lower edge of the blue shutter. The right shoe starts 48 mm behind its working plane, its orange slide handle exposed. The single spring-backed orange proof block starts at the left white mark on a captive cross rail. A green pushbutton starts a downstroke. Complete part dimensions and joint stops are in the included USD and README.
scoring: 0 after any 15 mm witness compression, active-cycle robot assistance, guide failure, moving a registered witness out of its 6 mm test band during a cycle or falsely triggering reversal. Otherwise .25 for a seated cassette (within 3 mm) and at least one proved site. For each proof, descend at least 50 mm, compress that site's shoe at least 2 mm against the block (normal contact at least .04 N), reopen at least 65 mm, and return within .5 mm of the top. For 1, prove both sites and maintain the seated cassette, open door, released button (<2 mm travel) and clear working parts for .5 s. Other outcomes score 0.
reset_notes: Rebuild the fixed fixture with the shutter open, right cassette displaced +48 mm, block at the +66 mm mark and button released. Use seed 0 and object_jitter=0.
fidelity: The captive trainer uses rigid components with passive guides and explicit spring travel for local edge and proof-block compression. An ideal kinematic motor and displacement switches approximate the actuator and contact strip. The two sampled sites represent a segmented edge. Values characterize this trainer. They do not establish human injury limits or compliance of a field installation.
